title: "Judge alignment within children"
output: html_document

Visualizes alignment across the within-child trials over age, excluding interference trials.

Figures are written to `../figures/withinchild_*_<version>.png`. The
`withinchild_` 

Conventions follow `11_visualize_alignment_test_pairs.Rmd`: run from `analysis/`, paths
relative to it, `theme_bw()`, `reorder_within` + `scale_y_reordered` for
per-facet ordering, `ggsave(..., "../figures/...")`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)
library(tidytext)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.retina = 2)

PROMPT_VERSION <- "v6"   # bump alongside 10_judge_alignment_test_pairs.py
RAW_ALPHA      <- 0.3

PAL2 <- c("#4B0F6B", "#F06BA8")

judgments <- read_csv("../data/judgments/alignment_within_child.csv") %>%
  filter(prompt_version == PROMPT_VERSION, !is.na(score),
         draw_interference == 0, utterance_interference == 0)

fig_path <- function(stem) {
  sprintf("../figures/withinchild_%s_%s.png", stem, PROMPT_VERSION)
}

# Adults run to 28 years and children stop around 12, so a single continuous axis
# spends half its width on 116 adult trials. Every age figure is therefore drawn
# twice: once over everyone, once over children alone, where the developmental
# range is actually readable.
children <- filter(judgments, is_child)

cat("rows:", nrow(judgments), "| prompt:", PROMPT_VERSION, "\n")
cat("participants:", n_distinct(judgments$participant_id), "\n")
cat("children:", nrow(children), "trials from",
    n_distinct(children$participant_id), "participants\n")
cat("age range:", sprintf("%.1f-%.1f yrs", min(judgments$age_yrs), max(judgments$age_yrs)), "\n")
count(judgments, target_category)
```

## 1.Overall score distribution (children only)

```{r score-distribution, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
p_dist <- ggplot(children, aes(score)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, fill = PAL2[1], colour = NA) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-2.5, 102.5), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of within-child alignment scores",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d trials; %.0f%% at 100, %.0f%% at 0",
                       nrow(children),
                       100 * mean(children$score >= 100),
                       100 * mean(children$score <= 0)),
    x = "Alignment score (0-100)", y = "Trials"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

p_dist
ggsave(fig_path("score_distribution"), p_dist, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

```{r score-by-category-table}
judgments %>%
  group_by(target_category) %>%
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    mean       = round(mean(score), 1),
    median     = median(score),
    at_ceiling = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(score >= 100)),
    at_floor   = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(score <= 0)),
    agree_rate = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(referents_agree, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )
```

## 2. Alignment score by age

### All participants
```{r age-alignment-overall, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
age_score_plot <- function(dat, subtitle) {
  means <- dat %>%
    group_by(age_yrs) %>%
    summarise(score = mean(score), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(dat, aes(age_yrs, score)) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey55",
                fill = "grey80", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = age_yrs), alpha = .5, size = 1.8) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(end = 0.9, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    labs(title = "Within-artist alignment score by age",
         subtitle = subtitle,
         x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Alignment score (0-100)") +
    theme_bw()
}

p <- age_score_plot(
  judgments,
  sprintf("all categories pooled; %d trials, children and adults; grey line is a linear fit",
          nrow(judgments)))
p
ggsave(fig_path("age_alignment_overall"), p, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r age-alignment-children, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
p <- age_score_plot(
  children,
  sprintf("all categories pooled; %d child trials only; grey line is a linear fit",
          nrow(children)))
p
ggsave(fig_path("age_alignment_children"), p, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

## 3. Referent agreement by age

`referents_agree` is TRUE when the judge gave the drawing and the description the
same animal name, with "unclear" on either side counting as disagreement. It is a
coarser, more interpretable companion to the 0-100 score: not *how* aligned, but
whether the two modalities landed on the same animal at all.

A proportion needs grouping, so age is binned into six quantile bins (the same
`cut()` convention script 11 uses), each holding a similar number of trials.
Error bars are normal-approximation binomial 95% CIs. The curve is a logistic fit
through the raw 0/1 trials, not through the binned proportions, so it uses the
continuous age rather than the bin midpoints.

```{r age-bins}
N_AGE_BINS <- 6

# unique() on the breaks guards against tied quantiles collapsing a bin.
AGE_BREAKS <- unique(quantile(judgments$age_yrs,
                              probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = N_AGE_BINS + 1),
                              na.rm = TRUE))

agree_dat <- judgments %>%
  filter(!is.na(referents_agree)) %>%
  mutate(age_bin = cut(age_yrs, AGE_BREAKS, include.lowest = TRUE, dig.lab = 3),
         agree   = as.integer(referents_agree))

# normal-approximation binomial CI, clamped to [0, 1]. mid is the mean age of the
# trials actually in the bin rather than the bin's nominal midpoint: it keeps the
# black points on the same continuous axis as the logistic fit, and it stays
# correct if a quantile bin comes out empty or lopsided.
agree_ci <- agree_dat %>%
  group_by(age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), p = mean(agree), mid = mean(age_yrs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se    = sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n),
         lower = pmax(0, p - 1.96 * se),
         upper = pmin(1, p + 1.96 * se))

agree_ci
```

```{r age-referents-agree, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
p_agree <- ggplot(agree_dat, aes(age_yrs, agree)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = age_yrs), alpha = 0.15, size = 1.6,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.03, seed = 1)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"),
              se = TRUE, colour = "grey45", fill = "grey80", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = agree_ci, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                aes(x = mid, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                width = 0.3, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = agree_ci, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = mid, y = p), size = 3.4, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(end = 0.9, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.05, 1.05), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Referent agreement by age",
       subtitle = paste(sprintf("%d trials;", nrow(agree_dat)),
                        "black points are binned proportions with 95% CI,",
                        "curve is a logistic fit through the raw trials"),
       x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Drawing and description named the same animal") +
  theme_bw()

p_agree
ggsave(fig_path("age_referents_agree"), p_agree, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

Children only. Adults run to 28 and agree ~93% of the time, so on the pooled axis
above they flatten the interesting part of the curve into the left third.

```{r age-referents-agree-children, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
agree_kids <- filter(agree_dat, is_child)

# bins recomputed within children rather than reused from the pooled breaks, whose
# top two bins are almost entirely adults
KID_BREAKS <- unique(quantile(agree_kids$age_yrs,
                              probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = N_AGE_BINS + 1),
                              na.rm = TRUE))

agree_kids_ci <- agree_kids %>%
  mutate(age_bin = cut(age_yrs, KID_BREAKS, include.lowest = TRUE, dig.lab = 3)) %>%
  group_by(age_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), p = mean(agree), mid = mean(age_yrs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se    = sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n),
         lower = pmax(0, p - 1.96 * se),
         upper = pmin(1, p + 1.96 * se))

p_agree_kids <- ggplot(agree_kids, aes(age_yrs, agree)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = age_yrs), alpha = 0.15, size = 1.6,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.03, seed = 1)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"),
              se = TRUE, colour = "grey45", fill = "grey80", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = agree_kids_ci, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                aes(x = mid, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                width = 0.15, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = agree_kids_ci, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = mid, y = p), size = 3.4, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(end = 0.9, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.05, 1.05), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Referent agreement by age, children only",
       subtitle = paste(sprintf("%d child trials (adults excluded);", nrow(agree_kids)),
                        "black points are binned proportions with 95% CI"),
       x = "Age (yrs)", y = "Drawing and description named the same animal") +
  theme_bw()

p_agree_kids
ggsave(fig_path("age_referents_agree_children"), p_agree_kids,
       width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

## 4. What were drawings categorized as?

```{r drawing-referents, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
drawing_refs <- judgments %>%
  filter(!is.na(drawing_referent)) %>%
  count(target_category, drawing_referent) %>%
  mutate(correct  = drawing_referent == target_category,
         referent = reorder_within(drawing_referent, n, target_category))

p_draw_ref <- ggplot(drawing_refs, aes(n, referent, fill = correct)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ target_category, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL2, name = "matches target") +
  labs(title = "What Gemini called each drawing",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d within-child trials; faceted by the animal the child was asked to draw",
                          sum(drawing_refs$n)),
       x = "Number of trials", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

p_draw_ref
ggsave(fig_path("drawing_referents"), p_draw_ref, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

## 6. What is the confusion matrix of referents? Eg when a drawing was called a crab, what did the description get called?

### Only including the six target animals and "unclear" on either side, with everything else collapsed into "other". 

```{r referent-confusion, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=6}
CATS <- c("crab", "octopus", "whale", "shark", "seahorse", "turtle", "unclear")

LEVELS <- c(CATS, "other")

# expand_grid + left_join rather than complete(): the grid is built explicitly, so
# empty cells are guaranteed present and drawn as zeroes instead of as gaps in the
# tile layout.
counted <- judgments %>%
  filter(!is.na(drawing_referent), !is.na(utterance_referent)) %>%
  mutate(d = ifelse(drawing_referent   %in% CATS, drawing_referent,   "other"),
         u = ifelse(utterance_referent %in% CATS, utterance_referent, "other")) %>%
  count(d, u)

confusion <- expand_grid(d = LEVELS, u = LEVELS) %>%
  left_join(counted, by = c("d", "u")) %>%
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0L),
         d = factor(d, levels = LEVELS),
         u = factor(u, levels = rev(LEVELS)))

p_conf <- ggplot(confusion, aes(d, u, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, "")),
            size = 3, colour = ifelse(confusion$n > max(confusion$n) * 0.6,
                                      "white", "grey20")) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = "trials") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Drawing referent vs description referent",
       subtitle = "within-child trials; the diagonal is agreement",
       x = "Gemini's label for the drawing",
       y = "Gemini's label for the description") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))

p_conf
ggsave(fig_path("referent_confusion"), p_conf, width = 7.5, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

### How about every label?!

```{r referent-confusion-full, fig.width=13, fig.height=12}
ALL_LABELS <- sort(unique(c(judgments$drawing_referent,
                            judgments$utterance_referent)))
ALL_LABELS <- ALL_LABELS[!is.na(ALL_LABELS)]

# order: the six targets, then unclear, then the rest by total use across both
# modalities, so the busy corner of the matrix is top-left instead of alphabetical
rest <- setdiff(ALL_LABELS, CATS)
used <- c(judgments$drawing_referent, judgments$utterance_referent)
rest_freq <- names(sort(table(used[used %in% rest]), decreasing = TRUE))
FULL_LEVELS <- c(CATS, rest_freq)

counted_full <- judgments %>%
  filter(!is.na(drawing_referent), !is.na(utterance_referent)) %>%
  count(d = drawing_referent, u = utterance_referent)

confusion_full <- expand_grid(d = FULL_LEVELS, u = FULL_LEVELS) %>%
  left_join(counted_full, by = c("d", "u")) %>%
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0L),
         d = factor(d, levels = FULL_LEVELS),
         u = factor(u, levels = rev(FULL_LEVELS)))

p_conf_full <- ggplot(confusion_full, aes(d, u)) +
  # empty cells drawn as a faint ground rather than left white, so the grid stays
  # legible across 64 columns and a zero reads as "asked and not found"
  geom_tile(fill = "grey96", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_tile(data = filter(confusion_full, n > 0),
            aes(fill = n), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(data = filter(confusion_full, n > 0),
            aes(label = n, colour = n > 20), size = 1.9) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
                       name = "trials") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"),
                      guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Drawing referent vs description referent, every label",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste("%d within-child trials, %d distinct referents;",
                                "targets first, then by frequency.",
                                "Fill is sqrt-scaled."),
                          nrow(judgments), length(ALL_LABELS)),
       x = "Gemini's label for the drawing",
       y = "Gemini's label for the description") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

p_conf_full
ggsave(fig_path("referent_confusion_full"), p_conf_full,
       width = 13, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

judgments %>%

## 7. Age models

The slopes the figures above are showing, as numbers.

```{r models}
library(lmerTest) 

cat("\n--- alignment score ~ age (all participants) ---\n")
age_all_model <- lmer(score ~ age_yrs + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | target_category), data = judgments)
summary(age_all_model)

cat("\n--- alignment score ~ age (children only) ---\n")
age_children_model <- lmer(score ~ age_yrs + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | target_category), data = children)
summary(age_children_model)

cat("\n--- referents agree ~ age (logistic, all participants) ---\n")
agree_model <- glmer(agree ~ age_yrs + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | target_category),
                     family = binomial, data = agree_dat)
summary(agree_model)
```
